documents.title: IRIS
documents.text: IRIS is a neurosymbolic framework that combines LLMs with static analysis for security vulnerability detection. IRIS uses LLMs to generate source and sink specifications and to filter false positive vulnerable paths. At a high level, IRIS takes a project and a CWE (vulnerability class, such as path traversal vulnerability or CWE-22) as input, statically analyzes the project, and outputs a set of potential vulnerabilities (of type CWE) in the project.

documents.title: CWE-Bench-Java
documents.text: This repository also contains the dataset CWE-Bench-Java, presented in the paper LLM-Assisted Static Analysis for Detecting Security Vulnerabilities. At a high level, this dataset contains 213 CVEs spanning 49 CWEs. Some examples include path-traversal, OS-command injection, cross-site scripting, and code-injection. Each CVE includes the buggy and fixed source code of the project, along with the information of the fixed files and functions. We provide the seed information in this repository, and we provide scripts for fetching, patching, and building the repositories. The dataset collection process is illustrated in the figure below: The table below summarizes the number of CVEs in our dataset grouped by CWE category, with smaller categories (fewer than 5 CVEs) grouped together for compactness. CWE-ID CVE Count -------- ----------- CWE-22 60 CWE-79 38 CWE-94 23 CWE-78 13 CWE-502 7 CWE-611 6 CWE-200 5 CWE-287 5 CWE-400 5 Other CWEs (36 total) 51

documents.title: Manually Curated Source/Sink Annotations
documents.text: For 50 CVEs we manually extracted source and sinks for the vulnerabilities and marked them in the CodeQL format. We also provide results for LLMs ability to detect those source/sink pairs. We collected the associated CodeQL-style descriptors and metadata, including file paths, signatures, and line ranges, and stored them in a CSV file.

documents.title: Using Docker (Recommended)
documents.text: If you intend to configure build tools (Java, Maven, or Gradle) or CodeQL, follow the native setup instructions below.

documents.title: Step 1: Setup Conda environment
documents.text: If you have a CUDA-capable GPU and want to enable hardware acceleration, install the appropriate CUDA toolkit, for example: Replace 12.1 with the CUDA version compatible with your GPU and drivers, if needed.

documents.title: Step 2: Configure Java build tools
documents.text: To apply IRIS to Java projects, you need to specify the paths to your Java build tools (JDK, Maven, Gradle) in the dep configs.json file in the project root. The versions of these tools required by each project are specified in data/build info.csv . For instance, perwendel spark CVE-2018-9159 2.7.1 requires JDK 8 and Maven 3.5.0. You can install and manage these tools easily using SDKMAN!.

documents.title: Step 3: Configure CodeQL
documents.text: IRIS relies on the CodeQL Action bundle, which includes CLI utilities and pre-defined queries for various CWEs and languages ("QL packs"). We suggest using CodeQL version 2.23.2. If you already have CodeQL installed, specify its location via the CODEQL DIR environment variable in src/config.py . Otherwise, download an appropriate version of the CodeQL Action bundle from the CodeQL Action releases page. - For the latest version: Visit the latest release and download the appropriate bundle for your OS: - codeql-bundle-osx64.tar.gz for macOS - codeql-bundle-linux64.tar.gz for Linux - For a specific version (e.g., 2.23.2): Go to the CodeQL Action releases page, find the release tagged codeql-bundle-v2.23.2 , and download the appropriate bundle for your platform. After downloading, extract the archive in the project root directory: This should create a sub-directory codeql/ with the executable codeql inside. Lastly, add the path of this executable to your PATH environment variable: Note: Also adjust the environment variable CODEQL QUERY VERSION in src/config.py according to the instructions therein. For instance, for CodeQL v2.23.2, this should be 1.8.1 .

documents.title: Visualizer
documents.text: IRIS comes with a visualizer to view the SARIF output files. More detailed instructions can be found in the docs.

documents.title: Usage:
documents.text: 1. Configure paths : Edit config.json to point to your outputs and source directories 2. Start the server : Run python3 server.py 3. Open in browser : Navigate to http://localhost:8000 4. Select a project : Choose a project from the dropdown to load its analysis results 5. Filter and explore : Use the CWE and model filters to explore specific vulnerabilities

documents.title: Using Docker containers with IRIS
documents.text: IRIS supports using prebuilt Docker images published in Docker Hub that have all the dependencies installed for individual Java projects. It is designed to talk to the host Docker daemon so it can work with the CWE-Bench-Java project containers. To enable this, run the container with the host Docker socket mounted and DOCKER HOST set: Inside the running container you can then use the helper scripts to run the containerized pipeline end-to-end:
